These ten all condition on a different edge from the one being edited. I left out the same-edge ones (replacing `none`, deleting a conv, 1x1 → 3x3, pool → conv) because almost any model would propose them. The picks fall into three groups:

- **Saturation across parallel or serial paths:** a 3x3 conv elsewhere shrinks the gain from adding another 3x3 conv.
- **Floor effects:** a harmful edit costs more in a strong parent than in a weak one.
- **Dead-signal topology:** when edge 0 is `none`, node 1 outputs zeros, so a conv on edge 2 or 4 has nothing to work on.
